Motherhood
MUTH-er-hood
noun (the calling of the mother)
From “mother” (Old English modor) and “-hood” (state or condition); the God-given calling and honour of the mother in the bearing, nurture, and instruction of children.

Biblical Definition

Motherhood is the God-given calling and honour of the mother in the bearing, nurture, and instruction of her children—a high and holy vocation woven into the creation order and exalted throughout Scripture. The bearing of children is named a blessing, not a burden: “Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” The mother's labour is honoured: the virtuous woman's children arise up and call her blessed; the aged women are to teach the young women to love their husbands and to love their children; and the apostle says, in a much-discussed verse, that the woman “shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety”—the godly mother walking out her calling in faith. The dictionary marks motherhood as a chief and honourable sphere of a woman's service to God, against the spirit of the age. The first corruption is the feminist devaluing of motherhood, which treats childbearing and the nurture of children as a lesser, even oppressive, role to be escaped for the “real” fulfilment of career and self—despising the heritage of the LORD and the calling He honours. The dictionary names this a corruption of the creation design, in which the woman's glory in the home and in the raising of children is no demeaning but a dignity. The opposite error is the sentimentality that idolizes motherhood as a woman's only worth or makes it an idol, forgetting that her first calling is to fear and love God, of which faithful motherhood is one expression. The dictionary holds the biblical honour: motherhood is a holy vocation, the fruit of the womb a reward of God, the godly mother a builder of the house and a shaper of generations, who labours not for the praise of men but in faith, charity, and holiness before God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The God-given calling and honour of the mother in bearing, nurturing, and instructing children (Psalm 127:3; Titus 2:4); a holy vocation, against the feminist devaluing of motherhood and the sentimentality that idolizes it.

expand to see more

MOTHERHOOD, noun. [Old English modor.] The God-given calling of the mother in bearing and nurturing children.

Children are an heritage of the LORD, the fruit of the womb His reward (Psalm 127:3).

Her children arise up and call her blessed (Proverbs 31:28).

The aged women teach the young to love their children (Titus 2:4).

A holy vocation, against the devaluing of motherhood and its idolizing.

Key Scripture

Ps 127:3 — "Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward."

Pr 31:28 — "Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her."

Tit 2:4 — "That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,"

1 Ti 2:15 — "Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety."

Modern Corruption

Feminism devalues motherhood as a lesser, oppressive role to be escaped for career and self; the opposite sentimentality idolizes it as a woman's only worth. Both miss the holy vocation Scripture honours.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the honour of motherhood as a holy calling. The chief corruption of the age is the feminist devaluing of motherhood, which treats childbearing and the nurture of children as a lesser, confining, even oppressive role to be escaped for the “real” fulfilment of career and self-realization. The dictionary names this a corruption of the creation design and a contempt for what God calls a blessing: children are the heritage of the LORD and the fruit of the womb His reward, and the mother who bears and raises them in faith fills a vocation God Himself honours. Her glory in the home is no demeaning but a dignity.

The opposite error is a sentimentality that idolizes motherhood—making it a woman's only worth, or an idol of the heart, so that the childless or the single woman is counted a failure and the mother's identity rests wholly in her children rather than in God. The dictionary holds the biblical balance: motherhood is a high and honourable calling, but a woman's first calling is to fear and love God, of which faithful motherhood is one blessed expression. The godly mother labours not for the praise of men nor for her own fulfilment as an end, but in faith, charity, and holiness before God—a builder of the house, a shaper of generations, blessed by her children and praised in the gates.

Hebrew Roots

From the Old English modor (mother) and “-hood” (state or condition); the calling and honour of the mother, grounded in the creation blessing of fruitfulness.

expand to see more

Modor, Old English, mother, with “-hood,” the state or condition.

Grounded in the creation blessing: be fruitful and multiply (Genesis 1:28).

The fruit of the womb a “reward” (Hebrew sakar) of the LORD (Psalm 127:3).

The godly mother's children “call her blessed” (Proverbs 31:28).

A holy vocation within the complementary order of creation.

Usage

"The pastor honoured motherhood as a holy calling against the spirit that devalues it."

"He taught that children are a heritage of the LORD, not a burden to be escaped."

"She raised her children in faith, charity, and holiness, blessed in her high vocation."
